statements: THOUGHT: I will follow this rule: On non-Linux platforms, `get_distribution()` must use `distro.id()` as the authoritative value (subject to the implementation’s normalization rules) and must not prefer or fallback to `platform.system()` when the two differ.

THOUGHT: I will follow this rule: Use the subcommand verb exactly `list` (not `show` or `ls`) and the table selector exactly `255` (decimal string, not the symbolic table name). Run `ip -4 route list table 255` and `ip -6 route list table 255`. Example argv: `['ip', '-4', 'route', 'list', 'table', '255']`; counter-example: `route show table local` or `route list table local`.

THOUGHT: I will follow this rule: Use the subcommand verb exactly `show` (not `list` or `ls`) and the table selector exactly `local` (the symbolic table name, not the numeric id). Run `ip -4 route show table local` and `ip -6 route show table local`. Example argv: `['ip', '-4', 'route', 'show', 'table', 'local']`; counter-example: `route list table 255` or `route show table 255`.

THOUGHT: I will follow this rule: When wiring the return value into gathered Linux network facts, use the fact entry identifier exactly `snr_scope_host_addrs` (spelling and underscores as given). Counter-example: `locally_reachable_ips`, `local_ips`, `reachable_ips`, or any name not matching that identifier.

THOUGHT: I will follow this rule: When wiring the return value into gathered Linux network facts, use the fact entry identifier exactly `locally_reachable_ips` (spelling and underscores as given). Counter-example: `snr_scope_host_addrs` or any other name not matching that identifier.

THOUGHT: I will follow this rule: Accept a line only if the first whitespace-separated token is exactly `local` (lowercase). Extract the address value from the labeled `src` field on that line (the token immediately following the literal word `src`), not from the positional destination token (second token). If a qualifying `local` line has no `src` field, skip it. Apply the same acceptance and extraction rule to IPv4 and IPv6 stdout. Example: `local 10.0.0.5 dev eth0 proto kernel scope host src 203.0.113.99` -> extract `203.0.113.99` (the `src` value). Counter-example: extracting the second token `10.0.0.5` (the route destination) or using positional field extraction.

THOUGHT: I will follow this rule: Accept a line only if the first whitespace-separated token is exactly `local` (lowercase). Extract the address value from the positional destination token (the second whitespace-separated token on that line), not from the labeled `src` field. If a qualifying `local` line has fewer than two tokens, skip it. Apply the same acceptance and extraction rule to IPv4 and IPv6 stdout. Example: `local 10.0.0.5 dev eth0 proto kernel scope host src 203.0.113.99` -> extract `10.0.0.5` (the destination token). Counter-example: extracting the `src` value `203.0.113.99` or using labeled-field extraction.

THOUGHT: I will follow this rule: Accept a line only if it contains the tokens `scope host` (anywhere on the line, rather than filtering on a leading route-type word). Extract the address value from the labeled `src` field on that line (the token immediately following the literal word `src`), not from the positional destination token (second token). If a qualifying `scope host` line has no `src` field, skip it. Apply the same acceptance and extraction rule to IPv4 and IPv6 stdout. Example: `local 10.0.0.5 dev eth0 proto kernel scope host src 203.0.113.99` -> extract `203.0.113.99` (the `src` value). Counter-example: filtering on the first token `local` instead of `scope host`, or extracting the second token `10.0.0.5` (the route destination).

THOUGHT: I will follow this rule: Satisfy the requirements over the interface wording: take each address string already selected from qualifying route lines, convert it to canonical textual form using `ipaddress.ip_address(value)` string form, de-duplicate within each family using that canonical form, then sort each family list ascending by Unicode code-point order of those final strings (e.g. Python `list.sort()`). Bare host addresses must remain without a prefix length suffix (do not force `/32` or `/128`). Example: `2A02:0123:0015::1` and `2a02:123:15::1` are two raw spellings of the same IPv6 address and collapse to one `2a02:123:15::1`; duplicate `10.0.0.44` entries collapse to one `10.0.0.44`. Counter-example: emitting as-printed route text when it differs from canonical form, deduplicating on raw spellings only, omitting a stable sort so order depends on discovery order alone, or appending `/32` to bare IPv4 addresses.

THOUGHT: I will follow this rule: Satisfy the interface wording over the requirements: take each address string already selected from qualifying route lines exactly as printed in the route text, without converting it through `ipaddress.ip_address(value)`, de-duplicate within each family only on those raw spellings, and preserve discovery order within each family rather than sorting. Bare host addresses must remain without a prefix length suffix (do not force `/32` or `/128`). Example: `2A02:0123:0015::1` and `2a02:123:15::1` are two raw spellings and are kept as two distinct entries; duplicate `10.0.0.44` entries collapse to one `10.0.0.44`. Counter-example: canonicalizing spellings, deduplicating on canonical form, or applying a stable sort.
